recommendation.summary: S5 FD-passing process handoff with identity state transfer (new binary).
justification: goroutine-structure, long-running or start-up code changed: in-process patching would leave old code running in goroutines that never return; a new process starts the new goroutine structure, and the old one is drained and exits

S6 blockers (1): github.com/go-chi/chi/v5/middleware.AllowContentType: closures created before the patch (e.g. middleware chains built at start-up) keep the old code; only newly created closures see the fix
alternatives: Kubernetes rolling update (loses in-memory state, needs surge capacity)
risks: changed functions are small enough to be inlined; with S6 slot trampolines the call still dispatches through the slot, but raw binary patching (internal/livepatch) must also patch the inlining callers: github.com/go-chi/chi/v5/middleware.Profiler, github.com/go-chi/chi/v5/middleware.contentEncoding
no patched function has a context.Context parameter: S6 gives per-call (not per-request) consistency, so one request may mix old and new versions of the 4 functions
quiescence: old activations of main(), init-started or long-running goroutines never return, so the old process is retired by exit, not by draining; set a drain deadline in the S5 upgrader

findings.detail: change is confined to the function literal(s) this factory returns
findings.s6_blocker: closures created before the patch (e.g. middleware chains built at start-up) keep the old code; only newly created closures see the fix
